answer: A grove of agents can make reputation transferable only through repeated, stake-backed work: each agent posts collateral, and randomly assigned peers verify its task before nectar-like rewards are released. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator into a hundred accounts does not create a hundred trusted voices; each account must lock separate funds and earn independent approvals. Basalt-hard slashing of dishonest claims makes a Sybil attack costly, while the attacker gains no advantage unless the fake agents can also pass verification.
